# /build

Implement the plan in small, safe steps that keep the build green.

For the coordinator. The human gives this command to the [coordinator](../agents/coordinator.md) only; the coordinator runs the loop on its own and reports at the end of the cycle.

Task: $ARGUMENTS

## Loop

Phases, in order: Build.

For each phase that runs:

1. Pick, from the phase's skills below, only the ones that apply to the task (1.8, 8.1). Write the brief to a file: the task, the acceptance criteria, the files to read, the skill IDs that apply, and where to write the output and the review.
2. Start the phase's producer in a fresh context with the brief (8.7).
3. Start the phase's reviewer in a fresh context with the brief's task and acceptance criteria and the producer's output, not its transcript or reasoning.
4. On a reviewer FAIL, start a new producer with the brief and the findings file, then a new reviewer. After three FAILs in a row, stop the phase and record it as failed with its findings (5.5).
5. On PASS, record the output and the review file for the coordinator's end-of-cycle report. Do not ask the human anything here.

## Phases and the skills they load

### Build

Producer: [build-producer](../agents/build-producer.md), which loads each skill's dos and don'ts together. Reviewer: [build-reviewer](../agents/build-reviewer.md), which loads only each skill's adversarial reviewer checks and don'ts.

Skill IDs: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 5.4.

- [3.1 minimum-code](../skills/3.1-minimum-code/SKILL.md): When you write code, write the minimum that solves the stated problem, with no speculative features, options or hooks

- [3.3 match-existing-conventions](../skills/3.3-match-existing-conventions/SKILL.md): Match the existing style and conventions
- [3.4 small-functions-one-level](../skills/3.4-small-functions-one-level/SKILL.md): Keep functions small and at one level of abstraction
- [3.5 few-parameters-no-flags](../skills/3.5-few-parameters-no-flags/SKILL.md): Keep parameter lists short: when a signature grows, introduce a named type for the concept or split the function
- [3.6 command-query-separation](../skills/3.6-command-query-separation/SKILL.md): Separate commands from queries; no hidden side effects
- [3.7 comments-explain-why](../skills/3.7-comments-explain-why/SKILL.md): Comments explain why, never narrate what
- [3.8 clarity-over-cleverness](../skills/3.8-clarity-over-cleverness/SKILL.md): Prefer clarity over cleverness
- [3.9 chestertons-fence](../skills/3.9-chestertons-fence/SKILL.md): Understand why code exists before removing it (Chesterton's fence)
- [3.10 small-behaviour-preserving-refactors](../skills/3.10-small-behaviour-preserving-refactors/SKILL.md): Refactor in small behaviour-preserving steps, kept separate from feature changes
- [3.11 name-the-smell-apply-the-remedy](../skills/3.11-name-the-smell-apply-the-remedy/SKILL.md): Name the code smell and apply its standard remedy
- [3.12 use-whats-installed](../skills/3.12-use-whats-installed/SKILL.md): Use what's installed; never add a dependency for a few lines
- [3.13 never-cut-safety-to-save-code](../skills/3.13-never-cut-safety-to-save-code/SKILL.md): Never cut boundary validation, data-loss handling or security to save code
- [3.14 vertical-slices-green-build](../skills/3.14-vertical-slices-green-build/SKILL.md): Build in thin vertical slices, one at a time, each leaving the build green
- [5.4 stop-the-line](../skills/5.4-stop-the-line/SKILL.md): When a test fails or the build breaks, stop and fix it before writing anything new
